questions.question: In the decision that moved engine jobs to fibers, how large was each fiber's stack?

3.2 ms is the later figure after tide-band chunks.

questions.question: Measured on the alpha build, how often did Gull scripts crash after fiber migration?
traps: The rate is in the last paragraph, past the browse excerpt.
1,400 is the number of native bindings, not a crash rate.

questions.question: Over one tide turn, how many file opens did the 128 m cell layout perform?
traps: 600 is the old 256 m layout's figure.
196 is the number of resident cells.

questions.question: In the worst case of the low-tide save bug, how far inland did the terrain solver push a salvage chest?
traps: The distance is in the final paragraph, past the browse excerpt; 31 of 50 is the repro count.

questions.question: In the alpha playtest field captures of streaming pool behaviour, how often did players reverse direction on average?
traps: The figure is past the excerpt; 22% and 63% are reload reductions.

questions.question: At what rate does the fixed-point tide simulation step?

The 10 updates a second in the host-streaming finding describe network updates for a rejected option.

questions.question: How much does one fixed-point tide step cost on Meridian?
traps: A near-identical finding gives 0.9 ms, but for Skiff.

questions.question: On what date was the deadline-based streaming read scheduler accepted?
traps: The premise is false: the deadline scheduler is still proposed. 2026-08-14 is its creation date.

questions.question: What frame budget in milliseconds does the "Kestrel world streaming and simulation core" Effort set for Skiff's 40 Hz mode?

questions.question: What is the Gull script tick budget per frame on Skiff?
traps: 2.0 ms is Meridian's budget.

questions.question: On what date was the world streaming and simulation Effort paused?
traps: The premise is false: the Effort is active and nothing records a pause.

questions.question: Which cell size decision was in force at the vertical slice on 2025-12-15?
traps: 192 m cells came in April 2026; 256 m cells were replaced in November 2025.

questions.question: Which decision rejected the proposal to run engine jobs on fibers from the start?
traps: The later move to fibers did not reopen this proposal; it stays rejected by the first thread-pool decision.

questions.question: Which finding showed that giving reads for tide-exposed cells top priority was wrong?
traps: The blocker about untextured terrain is an Issue, not the invalidating finding.

questions.question: Which proposed decision answers the open blocker about inland terrain staying untextured during tide turns?
traps: The tide-priority decision caused the blocker; it does not answer it.

questions.question: Which decision mitigated the risk that 192 m cells split the navigation tiles?
traps: The 192 m cell decision created the risk; it did not mitigate it.

questions.question: Which finding was recorded as evidence when the risk that fiber stacks make crash dumps unreadable was realized?
traps: The Gull thread-local finding is about fibers too, but it is not this risk's evidence.

questions.question: Before the Zstandard codec proposal was reopened, which decision had rejected it?
traps: The current rejected_by link names the 1 MB dictionary decision, which rejected it the second time; the first rejecter is only in the reopen history.

questions.question: After the Zstandard codec proposal was reopened, which decision rejected it again?
traps: The original Kelp decision rejected it the first time, before the reopening.

questions.question: Which constraint directly replaced the original 2.0 GB streaming pool budget?
traps: Three live-looking records share the title; the current one adds the tide-band reservation and replaced the June cut, not the original.

questions.question: Which finding showed that the December measurement of sustained Skiff streaming reads was wrong?
traps: The I/O budget constraint was superseded, not invalidated, and it is not a finding.

questions.question: What sustained read rate does the current streaming I/O budget allow on Skiff?
traps: 220 MB/s is the superseded December budget.
The streaming pool budget has a near-identical title but limits memory, not reads.

questions.question: Which finding measured the cost that ruled out having the host stream tide heights to every peer?
traps: The strict-float finding ruled out a different alternative.

questions.question: Which decision resolved the blocker about crash triage stalling on unreadable fiber stacks?
traps: A retracted draft with a near-identical title is not the resolver.
The current job decision came later and did not resolve the blocker.

questions.question: Which compaction did the finding that hot reload drops suspended Gull coroutines invalidate?
traps: The finding also invalidates the reload prototype finding, but that is not a compaction.
The head compaction is not invalidated.

questions.question: What is the latest measured cold decode rate on Skiff for Kelp with a 1 MB dictionary?
traps: The head compaction and the superseded finding say 2.2 GB/s; firmware 3.2 changed it after the compaction was written.

questions.question: Which tide drift measurement was the current one on 2025-10-25?
traps: The 6-minute finding came on 2025-10-29; a retracted duplicate of it has a near-identical title.

questions.question: Which save format decision was in force at the vertical slice on 2025-12-15?
traps: The tide-phase deltas came in February 2026.

questions.question: What did the "Kestrel world streaming and simulation core" Effort decide about cross-platform cloud saves?
traps: No decision exists: the issue was deferred by a survey finding to a post-launch patch.

questions.question: Does the accepted Gull VM compile scripts to machine code at run time?
traps: The VM runs bytecode with no JIT because consoles forbid runtime code generation; the build-time C++ transpiler was rejected.

questions.question: Why did Kestrel retire fibers for engine jobs in April 2026?
traps: The Gull thread-local bug had already been handled by pinning Gull threads; the April reversal was driven by unreadable crash stacks and the continuation prototype.

questions.question: The accepted decision to hot-reload Gull functions by swapping bytecode rests on a finding that has since been invalidated. Which finding invalidated that support?
traps: The coroutine defect Issue has a near-identical title but is an Issue, not the invalidating finding.
The reload decision itself is still accepted, not invalidated.

questions.question: How many archetypes existed in the world used by the ECS iteration benchmark that the alpha-world recheck invalidated?
traps: 912 is the alpha world's archetype count.
The findings say only that one spawn template was used; the count is only in the attached profile.

questions.question: In the cold-cache Skiff codec benchmark, how fast did Zstandard decode geometry?

questions.question: What LZ4 decode rate did the cold-cache Skiff codec benchmark record?
traps: 3.8 GB/s is LZ4's warm-cache figure from the invalidated October benchmark; LZ4 was not rerun cold.

questions.question: In the Skiff streaming trace of a falling tide with 256 m cells, what share of the reads were textures?
traps: 30% is the share of a cell that changes when the tide falls, not a read share.

questions.question: The risk that delta saves outgrow console save slots was accepted on the strength of one measurement. In the data behind that measurement, how long does an 80-hour save take to load on Skiff?

questions.question: According to the log behind the finding that float tides drift apart between machines within 6 minutes, at what minute did the first walkable tile flip?

6 minutes is the rounded headline.

questions.question: Which job model decision was in force at the vertical slice on 2025-12-15?
traps: The current decision is a thread pool, so a reader may assume the slice used one; at the slice, jobs ran on fibers.
The early fiber proposal was rejected and never in force.

questions.question: Which job model decision was in force at alpha on 2026-03-02?
traps: Plain fibers were replaced in February by fibers with Gull pinned to dedicated threads; the return to a thread pool came in April.

questions.question: Which streaming pool budget constraint applied at alpha on 2026-03-02?
traps: All three versions share one title; the 1.6 GB cut came in June 2026, after alpha.

traps: The compaction titled 'after beta' was written on 2026-06-10.
The head at beta had already been invalidated, but it was still the head.

questions.question: The measurement that alpha content needs 6.2 ms of Gull time per frame prompted a build-time alternative to the VM. Which decision rejected that alternative?
traps: The transpiler did not answer the Gull VM question, so no sibling rule rejected it; the bytecode decision named it explicitly when accepted.
The tree-walking interpreter decision was superseded, not the rejecter.

questions.question: The accepted policy to evict cells by distance and tide forecast rests on a simulation. What reload reduction did field captures measure instead?
traps: 63% is the simulated figure, which was invalidated.
38% is LRU's share of tide-turn reloads that had just been evicted.

questions.question: The proposal to compile Gull to bytecode was rejected and later reopened. Which finding about the decision that had rejected it prompted the reopening?
traps: The register VM prototype finding came after the reopening.
The 1.8 ms interpreter finding came before the first rejection.

questions.question: The current streaming pool constraint descends from a cut that an earlier risk predicted. Who wrote that risk?
traps: Priya Natarajan wrote the notice of the cut and Kenji Arakawa wrote the constraints; the risk is Dara Whitlock's.

questions.question: Starting from the current job model decision, walk back through the decisions it replaced to the defect that forced Gull scripts out of the fiber pool. Who filed that defect?
traps: Rhea Valdés wrote the job decisions; the defect was filed by Marta Lindqvist.

questions.question: Why does Kelp remain the streaming codec after the cold-cache rerun showed Zstandard beating it on Skiff?
traps: The original Kelp decision still rests on the invalidated warm-cache benchmark; the reason Kelp survives is the 1 MB dictionary result, not that benchmark.

questions.question: Which job model decision was in force on 2025-10-01?
